best.plan_strategy: Attempt 1: replace the linear baseline with a boosted-tree ranking generator. Fit a single hist_gbdt on all 2,760 training rows (no internal early-stopping slice), median impute, no scaling (trees are scale-invariant), moderate capacity with a low learning rate and enough iterations to fit spambase's strongly interactive word/char-frequency structure. Goal metric is balanced_accuracy; leave the operating point at the default rule (no class_weight) since the 1.54:1 imbalance is mild, and read recall vs specificity and cut_headroom from the report to decide whether attempt 2 should move the cut or keep pushing the ranking.

critic.evidence: Iteration 1 (hist_gbdt, 500 iters @ lr 0.06, 31 leaves, l2=1.0) scored balanced_accuracy=0.9538 (95% CI 0.9392~0.9676) against the bar 0.9711 — the bar sits above the CI, so the shortfall of 0.0173 is real. The fit is saturated on train: train_balanced_accuracy=1.0, train_f1=1.0, train_val_gap=0.046179, i.e. the 500-iteration budget with no early stopping memorised all 2,760 rows. The remaining distance is on the ranking axis, not the operating point: cut_headroom=0.001379 (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut=0.9552, KS≈0.9104), only 8% of the 0.0173 still needed, and recall 0.9309 vs specificity 0.9767 means a class_weight move could at most buy that same 0.0014. roc_auc=0.9840 / pr_auc=0.9751 are already high, so the lever with room is capacity/regularisation inside this family, which has been tried at exactly one point (1 attempt, best 0.9538) — a family swap is not yet warranted with 4 iterations left, and no per-family ranking-ceiling span exists here to justify one. No dropped_hyperparams; train_time 4.6 s of a 600 s budget, so cost is not a constraint.
critic.direction: Stay in hist_gbdt and attack the ranking by curbing the perfect-train memorisation — cut per-tree capacity and raise regularisation while keeping the iteration budget (shallower trees, stronger l2, smaller leaves, feature subsampling via max_features), leaving preprocessing and the default cut untouched so the score is attributable to capacity alone.

critic.evidence: Iteration 2 (hist_gbdt, 800 iters @ lr 0.04, 15 leaves, min_samples_leaf 40, l2=10.0, max_features 0.6) scored balanced_accuracy=0.9474 (95% CI 0.9294~0.9610) against the bar 0.9711 — the bar sits outside that CI, so the 0.0237 shortfall is real. The paired Δ vs iteration 1 is -0.0064 (95% CI -0.0170~+0.0027, P(better)=0.072), so the regularisation prescription produced movement this slice cannot resolve from zero: it bought nothing, and the previous 'overfitting' diagnosis is now spent without a record gain. The regularisation did what it was asked — train_balanced_accuracy fell from 1.0 to 0.9914 and train_val_gap from 0.046179 to 0.044029 — yet the ranking did not improve: roc_auc 0.9840→0.9851 and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.9552→0.9530, i.e. the ceiling of this family's ranking actually did not rise, and the goal's ceiling arithmetic requires balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut ≥ 0.9711 (KS 0.9422) while hist_gbdt has now delivered 0.9552 and 0.9530 at two very different capacity points. Operating point is priced out: cut_headroom 0.0056 against 0.0237 still needed is at most 24% of the distance, and recall 0.9199 < specificity 0.9749 means the positive class only wants a little more weight — worth ~0.0056, not 0.0237. So 76% of the gap is on the ranking axis, hist_gbdt has been tried twice (max 0.9538) spanning nearly the whole plausible capacity range with the ranking ceiling flat at 0.953–0.955, and 3 iterations remain — enough to test a genuinely different ranking generator rather than a third point in the same space. No dropped_hyperparams; train_time 5.07 s of 600 s, so cost is not binding. Note the honest limit: no per-family ranking-ceiling span exists in this run yet, so I cannot claim a swap will clear 0.0813 of KS — but a third hist_gbdt capacity point is measurably worth ~0 here, whereas an untried family is the only lever left with any chance of raising balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut.
critic.direction: Leave hist_gbdt — two capacity points have pinned its ranking ceiling at 0.953–0.955, well under the 0.9711 the bar needs — and spend the next attempt on a different ranking generator, xgboost with row and column subsampling plus a mild positive-class weight to close the recall/specificity gap, keeping preprocessing (median impute, no scale) unchanged so the family swap is the only lever moved.
